title: Adaptive Deep Neural Network Inference Acceleration at Edge via Joint Dynamic Partitioning and Resource Scheduling

abstract: Deploying deep learning models on resource-constrained edge devices faces acute memory and latency bottlenecks. However, existing DNN partition schemes overlook dynamic wireless channel fluctuation and hardware runtime jitter, leading to severe tail latency in multi-tenant edge servers. We propose an adaptive runtime partition framework called EdgeSplit that formulates layer-level offloading as a constrained Markov decision process. Experimental results on NVIDIA Jetson Xavier and Raspberry Pi 4 show that our approach achieves a 38% reduction in 99th-percentile inference latency compared to static split baselines. However, the limitation is that the framework does not consider battery energy degradation during sustained bursty traffic. Future work will extend the optimization to energy harvesting environments and evaluate asynchronous multi-device cooperative inference.

abstract: Federated learning enables collaborative model training across distributed clients without raw data sharing. However, the fundamental bottleneck lies in communication overhead and extreme client device heterogeneity where stragglers degrade global model convergence speed. We propose FedPruneQ, a joint structured pruning and mixed-precision quantization algorithm that dynamically adapts client sub-model capacities to local wireless uplink bandwidth. Extensive simulations on CIFAR-100 and FEMNIST demonstrate an 8.4x reduction in total uplink transmission bytes while maintaining top-1 accuracy within 1.2% of uncompressed FedAvg. A major limitation of this work is the assumption of independent and identically distributed channel states between training rounds. Future research must address non-stationary communication channels and Byzantine client poisoning resilience.

abstract: On-device model personalization is critical for privacy-sensitive IoT deployments, yet embedded microcontrollers have SRAM budgets below 512 KB, rendering standard backpropagation impossible. However, the challenge of activation memory footprint during backward passes remains unresolved for sub-megabyte devices. We introduce TinyReversible, an ultra-compact reversible neural network architecture and runtime that reconstructs activations on-the-fly, reducing peak SRAM utilization by 6.2x during fine-tuning. Empirical validation on STM32F7 microcontrollers demonstrates successful transfer learning under 256 KB SRAM constraints with an inference throughput of 14 FPS. Nevertheless, a critical limitation is that computational overhead increases total training energy consumption by 22%, making it unsuitable for battery-less ambient IoT nodes. Future work plans to explore intermittent computing integration and hardware-aware sparse backpropagation.

abstract: Hierarchical edge-cloud architectures bridge latency-sensitive edge processing and capacity-rich central cloud data centers. However, decentralized task scheduling across non-cooperative edge servers and base stations suffers from severe coordination overhead and partial observability bottlenecks. We propose a decentralized multi-agent deep deterministic policy gradient (MADDPG) framework with shared attention mechanisms that allows autonomous edge nodes to negotiate workload distribution without centralized telemetry. Evaluation against real Google cluster traces shows 24% lower task drop ratios and 19% improved edge bandwidth utilization. However, a key limitation is the vulnerability to non-stationary policies when edge nodes join or leave dynamically in ad-hoc mobile networks. Future work will investigate zero-shot transfer learning across heterogeneous topologies and formal safety constraints using control barrier functions.

abstract: Synchronous federated aggregation suffers from severe straggler delays in wide-area edge networks characterized by packet loss and intermittent device dropouts. However, naive asynchronous federated updates suffer from stale gradient divergence and catastrophic forgetting on non-IID client partitions. We present AsyncEdge-FL, an asynchronous aggregation mechanism incorporating staleness-damped exponential weighting and Lyapunov-guided client sampling. Testbed evaluations across 50 Raspberry Pi edge nodes show 3.1x faster wall-clock convergence time compared to FedAsync while matching centralized model accuracy. The primary limitation of this work is that it assumes trusted edge aggregation servers and does not provide formal differential privacy guarantees. Future work will integrate homomorphic encryption and investigate decentralized peer-to-peer gossip aggregation without parameter servers.

title: Energy-Aware Task Offloading and Resource Allocation for Battery-Constrained Edge AI Devices
venue: IEEE Transactions on Green Communications and Networking

abstract: Prolonging device operational lifetime is the paramount challenge for battery-powered IoT and wearable edge devices running continuous neural inference. However, existing energy-efficient offloading heuristics treat energy consumption and task deadline satisfaction as decoupled objectives, failing under non-linear battery discharge characteristics. We formulate a joint dynamic voltage-frequency scaling (DVFS) and wireless transmission power control model as a mixed-integer non-linear program (MINLP), solved via low-complexity geometric programming approximation. Experimental results on energy-harvesting IoT nodes demonstrate a 41% reduction in cumulative energy dissipation while meeting 95% of hard real-time latency deadlines. However, the limitation is that the framework requires exact knowledge of battery internal resistance and temperature curves, which drift over battery aging cycles. Future work will explore online reinforcement learning for battery state-of-health estimation and adaptive policy tuning.

abstract: Function-as-a-Service (FaaS) simplifies deploying modular AI services across edge-cloud topologies. However, cold start initialization latencies in containerized runtimes exceed 500 ms on edge nodes with limited I/O throughput, violating interactive SLA requirements. We design WarmEdge, a predictive function pre-warming and snapshot restoration architecture that employs temporal graph neural networks to forecast invocation chains across edge microservices. Benchmarked on a 16-node heterogeneous edge cluster, WarmEdge eliminates 76% of cold starts and reduces median pipeline latency by 45%. The core limitation is memory thrashing when total pre-warmed snapshot sizes exceed available edge RAM during bursty traffic spikes. Future research will explore hierarchical snapshot tiering to NVMe storage and zero-copy shared memory IPC between FaaS invocations.

abstract: Vision Transformers (ViTs) deliver superior spatial-temporal representation for intelligent video surveillance, yet quadratic self-attention complexity severely inhibits deployment on embedded edge accelerators. However, existing token pruning techniques induce temporal flicker and inconsistent object tracklets across sequential video frames. We develop TemporalTokenSlim, an edge-centric spatial-temporal token pruning mechanism with token recovery caches and 4-bit integer weight-activation quantization. Evaluated on NVIDIA Jetson Orin Nano, the model achieves 28.5 FPS real-time object tracking at 12W power envelope with minimal mAP loss (0.8%). The primary limitation is that the token recovery cache requires dedicated SRAM buffers that scale linearly with video resolution, creating bottlenecks on Ultra-HD streams. Future work will investigate sparse linear attention mechanisms and hardware-software co-design with emerging NPU architectures.

abstract: Industrial IoT (IIoT) sensors monitor heterogeneous machines with distinct operational dynamics and private telemetry. However, single-model federated learning performs poorly across divergent machine types, while negative knowledge transfer corrupts task-specific feature representations. We formulate a federated multi-task learning architecture based on clustered personal encoders and secure parameter sharing via differential privacy. Tested on multi-facility vibration and temperature datasets, our approach achieves 15% higher fault classification accuracy compared to standard federated baselines. The limitation is that computing pairwise task similarity matrices introduces an O(N^2) communication bottleneck as the number of IIoT devices scales to thousands. Future work will explore hierarchical cluster representatives and decentralized discovery of cluster affiliations without central coordination.

title: Resilient Consensus Protocols for Geo-Distributed Edge Infrastructure under Intermittent Connectivity
venue: IEEE International Conference on Distributed Computing Systems

abstract: State machine replication across geo-distributed edge clusters is essential for consistent metadata management. However, classical Paxos and Raft protocols suffer catastrophic availability loss during wide-area network partitions and frequent edge node churn. We propose EdgePaxos, a partition-tolerant consensus protocol utilizing conflict-free replicated data types (CRDTs) for local operations and speculative quorum commits during network reconvergence. Empirical evaluation across 8 cloud regions and 24 edge nodes demonstrates a 4x reduction in commit latency and zero downtime during simulated transatlantic cable cuts. However, a major limitation is that state convergence under high conflict rates incurs substantial storage overhead from tombstone accumulation. Future work will investigate garbage collection protocols tailored for resource-constrained edge storage and formal verification of CRDT merge safety under Byzantine failures.
